reviewEvidence: Approved against revision-5ad6d8b9, the repair of revision-9745e692. The review of the ORIGINAL revision was an INDEPENDENT adversarial pass by a fresh-context agent with no memory of the implementation, briefed to falsify four named claims (that a v1 session log restores exactly as before; that a stale container ID can never be trusted; that a failed or cancelled `use` never engages, and the converse that a successful one cannot fail to engage; that an explicit selection can never be clobbered by auto-selection), to check every acceptance criterion against the code rather than the tests, to sweep for stale consumers of the changed shapes, to run the security profile, and to attack the new JSONC scanner with hostile input. It earned its cost: it PROVED an AC-4 regression the author's own tests could not see (they only ever called the reconciliation with a configuration hint), and its clean findings are worth recording — v1-only logs restore identically through the real reader path, every store write is either membership-tested or the now-atomic auto-select, no `--config` path can be smuggled (all candidates are validated by `resolveConfigCandidate`/`candidatesOf`), and the host-exec / stop / remove gates are untouched. The blocking finding and the majors/minors were fixed in commit 6ff66c3 and are re-verified here: the reconciliation now carries the current selection's configuration when the caller supplies none (per workspace; an explicit hint still wins; nothing crosses workspaces), which is pinned by three new tests including the `/ws/project-a` + named-`python` case the reviewer used to demonstrate the regression; `allowsAutoSelection(decision)` gates the extension's auto-select hook so `/devcontainer off` holds in-session and not just across a reload; an unreadable configuration is reported like an unparsable one; an unterminated block comment is a syntax error instead of swallowing the rest of the file; the AC-8 race test now reproduces the production ordering with a real await gap; and the design no longer cites a test file that does not exist. The separate claim that a failed `use` persists evidence that would engage the session after a reload was traced and found NOT to hold (the ambiguous and no-candidate paths return before `applySelection`), and is now pinned by an assertion that the persisted list stays empty. Verification of this revision: `npm run typecheck`, 32 files / 387 unit tests, `verify-package.mjs --unit-tests` (all gates), a rebuilt `dist/` that matches a fresh build, the packed `smoke-pi-package.mjs --no-model`, and `npm run install:local -- --check`; `kata-cli verify` reports all nine acceptance criteria PASS. Process note recorded for the next phase: the repair originally sealed a revision whose own gate then rebuilt `dist/` AFTER hashing the owned paths, superseding the revision instantly — rebuild and commit `dist/` BEFORE sealing whenever `src/` changes.

findings.message: LIMITATION, RESTATED. Four behaviours live in the extension's command dispatch, which this repository has no unit harness for: delivering a handler's rendered result, draining the discovery diagnostics, the engagement gate, and reading the workspace configuration (which now reports both parse and read failures). Their policy halves are unit-tested (`displayCommandResult`, `reportDiscoveryDiagnostics`, `allowsAutoSelection`, `readConfigFacts`) and the wiring rests on the packed smoke run; a change to the dispatch must be smoke-checked rather than trusted to the unit suite.

RECORDED. The diagnostic sink is drained by the `/devcontainer` dispatch — the one surface with a guaranteed UI. A diagnostic raised by the per-turn execution context (an unparsable or unreadable configuration disabling the host guard) therefore reaches the operator at the next `/devcontainer` command, not immediately; the sink dedupes, so it is reported once. The Pi hooks that could drain it per turn (`before_agent_start`, `tool_call`) are not given a command context to notify with, so closing this properly means a different reporting channel, not a bigger drain.

RECORDED. The converse of AC-6: a successful `up` whose refreshed registry does not know the workspace leaves the session dormant (no engagement), where the old code engaged unconditionally. Engaging would be wrong — `bind()` would refuse — and the operator is not left guessing: the `up` result reports `selection: <status>`, which reaches them now that command output is actually delivered (Phase 2's fix).

RECORDED. When a configuration declares no `workspaceFolder`/`workspaceMount`, there is no mapping to exclude against, so every absolute mount target is reported as container-only — including a bind that in fact covers the workspace. It is a prompt fact, not a guard, and erring toward "the host may not see this" is the safe direction; guessing the CLI's default workspace target would fabricate a fact instead.

RECORDED (pre-existing). A still-listed but stopped candidate passes the membership test while `selectionFor` stamps the entry's state, so `bind()` can report `selected-valid` for a stopped container; the adapter then hands the CLI `--container-id <stopped>` and the CLI fails. No wrong-container risk (the id is real) and the failure is typed; a later pass could cross-check the candidate's state instead.

PROCESS LESSON, recorded because it cost a full re-seal cycle. The repair changed `src/` without rebuilding `dist/`; the seal's own gate then rebuilt `dist/` AFTER hashing the owned paths, so the revision superseded itself immediately and `verify` reported `revision_superseded` for all nine criteria. Rebuild and commit `dist/` BEFORE sealing whenever anything under `src/` or `extensions/` changes — the same rule the CHANGELOG/README hygiene already implies, now with the failure mode named.
